Q: Not getting the text above the images A:

You have z-index: -1 on the .container, so everything inside it (including the h1) goes behind other elements.

That’s why your text is appearing behind the images.
.container{ z-index: -1; }

and keep the negative z-index only on the images if you want them behind the text.
You can also add:
h1{ z-index: 1; }

so the heading stays above the background images.

Q: What is the optimum precision to use in an arithmetic encoder? A:

I investigated this years (decades) ago using 64-bit arithmetic coder and 64-bit range coder implementations.

The key conclusion is that the biggest benefit of moving from 32-bit to 64-bit arithmetic or range coding is not improved arithmetic precision itself, but the improved probability-model precision with far less rescaling.

The results show two separate effects:

  1. Better numerical precision in the coder itself gives only small compression gains, mostly visible on large files.

  2. More interestingly, with 64-bit coders, the frequency counts no longer need aggressive rescaling/halving, so probabilities can be represented far more accurately. That produces noticeably better compression on statistically stable data.

The practical implication is:

  • 32-bit coders force modeling compromises because cumulative frequencies must stay within tight bounds.

  • 64-bit coders remove most of those constraints.

  • Without those constraints, model design decisions can be based on source statistics rather than integer-overflow limitations.

Full results and source code here: https://sachingarg.com/compression/entropy_coding/64bit/

Q: How does the C compiler detect which function to start first? A:

When linked normally, a C program will begin execution at the function named main. Note that the prototype you're using for main is not one of the allowed forms. You're also using incomplete prototypes (if a function takes no arguments, you should place void in the parameter list).
